Site Identity

Basic information about this website.

Brand Colors

Your two main brand colors. Pick them here and click Apply, and they’ll be used across every page of your site. They start from the colors your site already uses, so you can adjust from there.

Fonts

The fonts for this whole site, in four groups: everything, paragraphs, headings and buttons. Set them once here and every page uses them, including pages you add later. Most designs set fonts on individual pieces, so Fourge overrides those pieces too; icons are left alone, since icon sets draw their symbols from a font of their own.
Save & Publish stores the choice, and any page you edit from then on picks it up on save. Use this button to sweep the pages nobody has opened since.

Heading Styles

Choose the font, size, weight, alignment, and color for your headings across the whole site. Headings are the titles on your pages — H1 is the main page title, H2 the section titles, and so on down to H6. Leave any box empty to keep what your design already uses. (A single page can still set its own heading look in that page's settings.)

Custom CSS

Advanced: your own CSS rules, applied to every page on the site. Anything you write here wins over the fonts and heading styles above, so use it for one-off tweaks the rest of Design doesn't cover. Leave it blank if you don't need it.
Save & Publish stores it, and any page you edit from then on picks it up on save. Use this button to sweep the pages nobody has opened since.

Favicon

The small icon shown in browser tabs, bookmarks, and search results. Upload a square image (512×512 PNG recommended; SVG, ICO, JPG, and WebP also work). It's saved to the site root as /favicon, the tab / Android / iPhone sizes are generated automatically, and it's applied to every page instantly — new pages pick it up when saved. Replacing it publishes under a fresh address, so browsers can't keep showing the old icon.

Contact Info

Social Profiles

SEO Platform — Import package

Deploys a deploy-<site>-<date>.json package from the 44i SEO platform: page titles & descriptions, JSON-LD schema, social tags, robots/llms files, redirects, security headers, and scheduled content. Preview first — it reports exactly what would be applied, skipped (with the reason), and left for a human, and writes nothing. Applying backs up every file it changes to data/bak/. Re-importing the same package updates in place instead of duplicating.
Automated delivery (optional)
Let the platform POST packages straight to this site. It authenticates with a per-site key (Bearer token) stored encrypted on the server — never in a public file.
AI auto-fix
Fills the gaps an audit grades, using this site's Anthropic key: page titles and meta descriptions that are missing or the wrong length, images with no alt text, internal links to the pages a campaign is targeting, and FAQ content for pages that have none at all. It only ever fills gaps — a title, description or FAQ that's already there is never touched. Runs on its own, once a day, by default — that's the point: a fix that only happens when someone remembers to click something keeps getting missed. Turn it off below if you'd rather trigger it by hand.
Each run covers up to 10 pages of metadata, 8 pages of image alts, 10 internal links, and 4 pages of FAQ content, so it stays quick and cheap. Anything left over is picked up next time.

Analytics

Google Analytics 4, Tag Manager, and Ads tracking — with live data and monthly reports.

Loading…

Reports auto-generate for the previous month when you open this tab.

1 · Tracking IDs

Enter any combination — the snippet adapts. GA4 fires via gtag.js; GTM loads the container; the Google Ads tag piggybacks on gtag.

2 · Reporting API (live data & reports)

Dashboard and reports read from the GA4 Data API using a Google Cloud service account. One-time setup:

  1. Google Cloud Console → create/select a project → enable Google Analytics Data API
  2. IAM → Service Accounts → create one → Keys → Add key → JSON
  3. Paste the downloaded JSON below
  4. GA4 Admin → Property Access Management → add the service account email as Viewer
Checking…

3 · Custom code (header & body)

Paste any extra tracking or script snippets beyond GA4/GTM/Ads. Header code is injected into <head>; body code just before the closing </body>. They're grouped by purpose (to line up with a consent banner) but all load today. Saving publishes them to every page automatically.

4 · Chatbot

Paste the chatbot embed code (from the CRM's chat-widget setup). It's injected into the <head> of every page. Use Chatbot in testing while you're still tuning it: the widget then stays completely hidden from real visitors and only appears for someone who adds ?chatbot=true to the address — it stays visible for the rest of that person's browsing session, and ?chatbot=false turns it back off.

GitHub Integration

Repo is read from data/site.json. The token is stored encrypted on the server — page saves and revisions mirror to GitHub for every editor, from any browser.
Needs repo scope.

Repository Override

Manually set GitHub repo if data/site.json hasn't been configured yet.

Markup API Key

Powers Markup generation (SEO + block extraction). Visible to the Architect account only.

Custom AI Endpoint

Optional — point Markup generation at a self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Open WebUI, Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM…) instead of the key above. Used only when all three fields below are set; clear any one of them (blank + Save) to fall back to the Markup API Key automatically. Visible to the Architect account only.

Contact-Form Email

Send a test email through the same transport your forms use (your SMTP relay, or the Mailgun API) to check delivery. Email is configured server-side in admin/config.secret.php. Submissions are always saved under Forms → Entries even if email fails.
Leave blank to send to your own account email (or the site's notify address).

Post-Launch Check

Run this after a site goes live. It audits everything the launch runbook covers — forms & reCAPTCHA, clean page addresses, crawlability, Google Analytics coverage, the sitemap, titles & meta descriptions on every page, and image alt text / unused media — then hands you the punch list of what still needs doing.

Launch: Domain Find & Replace

Going live? Swap every reference to the old (dev) address for the new domain — across all pages, blog posts, forms, SEO data, plugins, and site settings, in one pass. Scan first to preview exactly which files change and how many times; nothing is written until you approve it. Changed files are backed up to data/bak/, and the sitemap + robots file are rebuilt afterward. Tip: enter addresses without https:// (e.g. dev-client.44interactive.com → www.clientdomain.com) so every form of the link is caught.

Google Reviews

Pull reviews from this business's Google listing, keep them here, and choose which ones appear on the site. Add the Reviews block to any page in the page editor — it reads from this list, so hiding a review or fetching new ones updates every page without re-saving them.

Google connection

The API key is stored encrypted on the server and is never sent back to the browser or written into any public file. Only the server calls Google with it.
Checking…
The ID of this business's Google listing. Press Find if you do not have it.
Used for the “Leave a review” / “See all reviews” link on the block.

What shows on the site

Applies on top of the individual show/hide switches below.
Newest first. Leave blank for all of them.

Key safety

The key is encrypted on the server and never sent to a browser — but two things are worth proving rather than assuming: that the files holding it cannot be downloaded, and that the key would be useless to anyone who got it anyway.

Saved reviews

Google's API hands back at most five reviews at a time, and picks which five. Every fetch is merged into this list rather than replacing it, so the collection grows as Google rotates them — and your show/hide choices are never overwritten.

Map

Locations with a pin and a popup — dealers, clinics, campuses, service areas, or points on an image you upload. Add the Map block to any page in the page editor; it reads this list when the page loads, so fixing an address or hiding a location updates every map on the site without re-saving pages.

Where the map comes from

All three draw the same pins and the same popups. Only the background changes.

Google Maps key

Unlike the reviews key, this one cannot be hidden. Google's map runs in the visitor's browser, so the key is in the page for anyone to read — that is how the product works, not a flaw in Fourge. What makes it safe is restricting it, which takes a minute:

In Google Cloud Console → Credentials → your key:
• Application restrictions → Websites → add yourdomain.com/* and www.yourdomain.com/*
• API restrictions → Maps JavaScript API only
• Billing → Budgets & alerts → set a cap so a scraped key cannot run up a bill

With those three in place a copied key does nothing on anyone else's site. Leave this blank and the map quietly uses OpenStreetMap instead.
Saved in data/map.json, which is a public file — deliberately, because the page needs it.

Map image

Any image works. Bigger is better — visitors can zoom in, and a small image goes soft when they do.

Map tiles — advanced

The default is OpenStreetMap's public tile service, which is free and fine for a normal business site. If a map ever gets heavy traffic, paste a tile URL from a provider here instead — the map itself does not change.
Required by most tile providers, OpenStreetMap included.

How the map opens

1 is the whole world, 15 is a neighbourhood, 18 is a street.

Categories

A colour and a marker, set once and shared by every pin that uses it — so restyling forty locations is one edit. With two or more, visitors get a legend they can click to filter, and a page can carry a map of just one category.

Pins

Each pin is a set of fields, not a piece of code — which is what lets the same pins fill the popup, the location list under the map, and the structured data search engines read. Need something the fields do not cover? Add it under Extra fields.

Popup design

One template for every pin. {{title}}, {{subtitle}}, {{address}}, {{phone}}, {{url}}, {{image}} and any extra field as {{custom.hours}}. Wrap a part in {{#phone}}…{{/phone}} and it disappears for pins that have no phone. {{{body}}} keeps the HTML in the description; everything else is escaped, and scripts are stripped.
Applies to every map on the site. Prefix rules with .fourge-map so nothing leaks into the rest of the page.
Worth keeping: it is what screen readers and search engines read, and it is the only part of the map that works with no JavaScript at all.

Where the map appears

In the page editor, click a section and press Insert map. You can pick which categories that particular block shows, so a city page can carry only its own locations.

The map is always live. The written location list and the structured data are stamped into a page when it is saved — press this after a round of pin edits to bring them up to date everywhere without opening the editor.
Link /events in your nav once the pages are created. Give each page its own look under Pages → Page Settings → Custom CSS.
